messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing slow widget/chart loads on canary v5.12 for some orgs, e.g. org=849. Charts taking 2–4s to render vs ~200ms before. Anyone else seeing this?

jenny: seeing it locally against prod-canary for that org. Devtools shows main thread blocked ~2.8s during eval/parse step, but network for /api/metrics/batch also spikes. :eyes:

simon: any infra/telemetry changes around the deploy window? Kibana shows a spike at 13:32 in /telemetry/ingest QPS.

eng-deploy-bot: deploy: canary rollout v5.12 started at 2026-03-20T13:28:15Z. ENV change: TELEMETRY_SAMPLING=1.0 (was 0.1). Canary nodes: 3/3.

olga: that telemetry sampling bump would multiply client events. Also routing/kv-cache metrics show prefix miss rate jump coincident with deploy. If clients send more payloads, backend aggregation could be slowing /api/metrics/batch which the console waits on.

jenny: quick check of kv stats (from infra debug): `curl -s "https://console.internal/api/kv/cache/stats"` -> text output: "prefix_miss:0.42, eviction_rate:0.12, hot_keys:7". Miss ratio up from ~0.03.

simon: additionally we switched canary route_policy to cost_first yesterday for some experiments — that may route metric aggregation to smaller clusters causing serialization/backpressure. Combined w/ telemetry spike could explain the tail latency.

maya: timeline looks plausible: (1) route_policy change -> narrower backend capacity for batch endpoint; (2) telemetry sampling increased -> >10x traffic to ingestion -> kv cache churn and batch endpoint latency -> console charts block waiting on /api/metrics/batch.

olga: mitigation suggestions: revert TELEMETRY_SAMPLING to 0.1 for canary immediately, add temporary server-side throttle on telemetry ingestion per-org, and add a short frontend fallback: if /api/metrics/batch >400ms return cached tile + mark as stale.

simon: opening rollback PR for the TELEMETRY env and will add a guard for route_policy to prefer latency_first for metric aggregation.

eng-deploy-bot: rollback initiated: canary v5.12 halted, redeploying v5.11 to canary nodes (3/3). ETA ~2m.

jenny: after rollback, org 849 charts back to normal in canary, render <300ms. Confirming on multiple sessions. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks. Action items for followup: 1) Add server-side rate limit on telemetry ingestion and a safety cap per org; 2) Add client-side timeout/fallback for /api/metrics/batch (400ms) and use cached tiles; 3) Add kv_prefix_miss_ratio metric and alert if >0.2; 4) Document telemetry gating and change window for canary. I'll open a ticket and assign.

simon: also recommend adding a canary check that simulates high client telemetry to surface backend backpressure before rollout.

sre-ops: noted — will create PD watch and add playbook. If we see similar regression in prod we will escalate.

maya: I'll file the postmortem and include perf traces and the commit that changed sampling. Thanks everyone for quick triage.
